register.name: New Zealand, early recovery after Tropical Cyclone Maila
register.detail: New Zealand Government · announced 9 July 2026 · New Zealand Disaster Response Partnership · about SBD 3.4 million
register.note: SBD 1.13 million each to ADRA New Zealand, Save the Children New Zealand and Caritas Aotearoa New Zealand
register.text: Further New Zealand funding for early recovery in Western and Choiseul provinces after Tropical Cyclone Maila. It pays for repairing homes, restoring food production and livelihoods, clean water and sanitation and getting children back to school, which serve the shelter, food, livelihood, water and education standards.

register.name: New Zealand, support to the National Disaster Management Office
register.detail: New Zealand High Commission · Emergency High Commission Fund · reported 17 April 2026 · activities to be completed by 30 June 2026
register.note: Response facilities SBD 147,898, logistics SBD 142,600 and deployment of the National Emergency Response Team SBD 38,250
register.text: New Zealand funding for the National Disaster Management Office’s response facilities, its logistics in Honiara and Munda, and the deployment of the National Emergency Response Team to the affected areas. A faster response to disasters protects the shelter, health and food standards when a cyclone strikes.

register.name: Recovery from Tropical Cyclone Maila
register.detail: World Bank · released 11 June 2026 · Catastrophe-Deferred Drawdown Option approved in 2023
register.note: Part of the government’s US$15 million (SBD 120 million) recovery plan, also supported by the ADB
register.text: Pre-arranged World Bank financing released after the State of Disaster declared in April 2026: Tropical Cyclone Maila affected about 150,000 people and damaged homes, 81 schools and 21 health facilities. The recovery plan it supports aims to reopen schools, restore health services and help communities rebuild, which serve the education, health and shelter standards.

register.name: Second Resilience Development Policy Operation
register.detail: World Bank · approved 19 December 2025 · project P511758 · budget support
register.note: Follows the first Resilience DPO with a Cat DDO of November 2023
register.text: World Bank budget support for reforms to improve fiscal management, create the enabling environment for private sector development and enhance resilience to climate change, natural disasters and health emergencies. It finances the budget as a whole; its resilience reforms bear on the health and shelter standards when disasters strike.

register.name: Accelerating Trade Facilitation in the Pacific
register.detail: World Bank · approved 9 September 2025 · project P508537 · regional project, US$9M listed for Solomon Islands
register.note: Trade facilitation across the Pacific
register.text: A World Bank regional project to accelerate trade facilitation in the Pacific, with US$9 million listed for Solomon Islands. Faster and cheaper trade bears on the livelihood standard.

register.name: Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 23 May 2025 · project P502591 · live 5 June 2025 · implemented by the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat
register.note: Split evenly between grants and credits; the World Bank lists a US$4.5 million commitment
register.text: IDA financing that keeps Solomon Islands connected to the global financial system, with a standby facility for emergency correspondent banking services and help with compliance and payment systems. Between 2011 and 2022 the nation saw a 57 percent reduction in correspondent banking services, and over 5 percent of GDP is tied to remittances, so it protects the livelihood standard for families who receive money from abroad.

register.name: Tina River Hydropower Development Project, IDA additional financing
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · committed May 2025 · commercial operation scheduled for February 2028
register.note: Physical construction of Components 1 and 2 was 28.19% complete at 31 December 2025
register.text: Additional IDA financing for the Tina River hydropower plant, which will feed renewable power into the Honiara grid. It serves the energy standard, the one furthest from reach in Solomon Islands, where a person uses about 134 kWh of electricity a year.

register.name: Community Access and Urban Services Enhancement Project II
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 15 October 2024
register.note: US$18.8 million undisbursed in the World Bank Group portfolio snapshot of 2026
register.text: Roads, drainage and services for communities.

register.name: Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Project, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 8 December 2023
register.note: Part of a US$125 million project funded by ADB, the World Bank, the Global Environment Facility and the European Union
register.text: Water and sanitation for Honiara and the towns.

register.name: First Solomon Islands Resilience DPO with a Cat DDO
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 30 November 2023
register.note: US$5.2 million undisbursed in the World Bank Group portfolio snapshot of 2026; its Cat DDO released US$5 million after Tropical Cyclone Maila
register.text: Budget support with funds that release when disaster strikes.

register.name: MIGA guarantees for the 20MW Tina River Hydropower
register.detail: MIGA · effective 31 January 2020 to 30 January 2040 · held by Korea Water Resources Corporation and Hyundai Engineering
register.note: Gross exposure of US$11.3 million for Korea Water Resources Corporation and US$2.8 million for Hyundai Engineering
register.text: World Bank Group political risk guarantees for the private sponsors that build and run the 20MW Tina River hydropower plant, covering expropriation, war and civil disturbance and breach of contract. They bring private capital to the energy standard, the one furthest from reach in Solomon Islands.

register.name: Tina River Hydropower Development Project (GCF FP044)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved 6 April 2017 · US$70M loan and US$16M grant · World Bank the accredited entity · completion estimated 22 June 2028
register.note: Total project value US$242 million, with US$155.88 million of co-financing
register.text: The Green Climate Fund’s loan and grant for the Tina River hydropower plant, which will reduce Honiara’s reliance on diesel generation. It serves the energy standard, the one furthest from reach in Solomon Islands.

register.name: Tina River Hydropower Development Project (IDA)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved fiscal year 2017 · project P161319 · US$13.9M undisbursed in the 2026 portfolio snapshot
register.note: Co-financed by the GCF, ADB, Australia, Korea’s Economic Development Cooperation Fund and the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development
register.text: The World Bank’s IDA financing for the Tina River Hydropower Development Project, which links a renewable power plant to the Honiara grid. It serves the energy standard, the one furthest from reach in Solomon Islands.

register.name: Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Project, second additional financing
register.detail: ADB · announced 11 December 2024 · Asian Development Fund grant · Greater Honiara, Auki, Gizo, Munda, Noro and Tulagi
register.note: Part of a US$125 million project funded by ADB, the World Bank, the Global Environment Facility and the European Union; also covers cost overruns
register.text: An ADB grant for the government’s water and sanitation sector plan: more piped water and sanitation, hygiene awareness, water conservation and better fecal sludge management in Greater Honiara and five towns. It serves the water and shelter standards; basic drinking water reaches 71.6% of the people.

register.name: Integrated Solid Waste Management Project for Climate- and Disaster-Resilient Honiara
register.detail: ADB · signed 8 November 2024, Honiara · $6.93M loan and $12.48M Asian Development Fund grant
register.note: The country’s first solid waste management project
register.text: ADB financing for a new controlled landfill for Honiara, the rehabilitation of the existing dump site and stronger waste services, with recycling and community livelihood programmes. Safer waste disposal serves the health and shelter standards in the capital.

register.name: Land and Maritime Connectivity Project
register.detail: ADB · $74.4M concessional loan and $74.5M Asian Development Fund grant · second tranche of $53M under way, October 2024 · government contribution $21.8M
register.note: Overall cost of almost $171 million
register.text: ADB financing for climate-resilient roads on the east–west corridor of Guadalcanal and for provincial wharves at Kira Kira and Ahanga, with marketplaces and passenger buildings. Roads and wharves that stay open all year connect communities to markets, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Development Policy Loan for Strengthening Fiscal and Economic Resilience
register.detail: JICA · signed 24 July 2026, Tokyo · 2.35% a year · repayment over 30 years with 10 years of grace · untied
register.note: Estimated programme cost ¥6,000 million
register.text: A Japanese ODA loan of budget support for reforms in domestic resource mobilization, public financial management and fiscal policy, good governance and economic growth. It finances the budget as a whole, which carries the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Australia, support to the National Transport Fund
register.detail: Australian Government · additional SBD 30 million signed 25 June 2026 · roads in Honiara and Malaita Province
register.note: Adds to earlier Australian support of SBD 60 million to the Fund
register.text: Australian funding through the National Transport Fund to maintain and repair key roads in Honiara and Malaita Province, with work for local contractors. Roads connect communities to markets, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Australia, support after Tropical Cyclone Maila and global energy shocks
register.detail: Australian Government · agreed at the Australia–Solomon Islands Leaders’ Meeting, 3 June 2026 · SBD 200 million
register.note: Australia also agreed to double training and vocational scholarships to 1,500 in 2027
register.text: Australian support to help Solomon Islands respond to Tropical Cyclone Maila and to the effects of global energy shocks. It bears on the shelter, health and education services the cyclone damaged, and on the energy standard, the one furthest from reach.

register.name: Australian development assistance to Solomon Islands, 2025–26
register.detail: DFAT · budget estimate 2025–26 · bilateral allocation A$103.6 million
register.note: Programmes named include Tina River Hydropower, the Australian Water Partnership and Pacific Women Lead
register.text: Total Australian official development assistance to Solomon Islands in the 2025–26 budget estimate, of which A$103.6 million is the bilateral programme. DFAT names programmes in hydropower, climate infrastructure, water and women’s leadership, which bear on the energy, water and livelihood standards.

register.name: Tina River transmission line
register.detail: Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific · 22-kilometre line from the Tina River site to the Honiara grid
register.note: Australia also signed a US$4.5 million equivalent grant for Tina River cost overruns
register.text: Australia’s investment in the 22-kilometre transmission line that links the Tina River hydropower plant to the Honiara grid and reduces the capital’s reliance on diesel generation. It serves the energy standard, the one furthest from reach in Solomon Islands.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Forest over nine tenths of the land: timber already exported, and carbon that could earn as it stands.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: More than 57,000 cubic metres of fresh water a person each year.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 36.6% are under fifteen: a young nation.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2024
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: Kastom Gaden Association
items.text: A local food and farming association that teaches organic gardening and nutrition; in 2026, with WorldFish, it trained 35 secondary students from six schools in Western Province in nursery management, composting, soil preparation and seed germination.

items.name: Sunpower Limited
items.text: A commercial and retail solar power provider that designs and distributes affordable solar home energy solutions, from portable solar lights to multi-light home systems, and in February 2025 began offering them to the members of SPBD Solomon Islands.

items.name: Kokonut Pacific Solomon Islands
items.text: A Honiara social enterprise, founded in 2004, that buys virgin coconut oil and cocoa beans from smallholders at fair prices and processes them into food, chocolate and cosmetic products, supporting over 1,000 farmers.

items.name: SPBD Solomon Islands
items.text: A microfinance provider that lends to women and helps them start, grow and keep micro-businesses; over 400 of its members attended its first Solomon Islands Businesswomen Awards in Honiara in June 2025.

items.name: Mselen
items.text: The mobile money service of Solomon Islands Telekom, developed with the UN Capital Development Fund, which signs up rural agents for mobile top-ups, utility payments and bulk payments and trains women market vendors to use it.
